passage:
Ujjwal put down his tea. "Parveen, the form is filled. Science with maths."
"Papa, may I ask why you chose it without asking me?"
"Because it is the best path. Look at Bhavesh, my cousin's boy. Big job, big flat."
"I'm happy for Bhavesh, Papa. But I like history and writing."
"History gives you what?"
"That's what I'd like to ask someone who knows. Can we meet the school counsellor together? I'll listen to the facts. I'm not saying no to you. I'm saying I have a mind."
Ujjwal was quiet for a moment. "Counsellor. Fine. Saturday. But you listen to me too."
"Always, Papa."

qa.q: Who does Ujjwal hold up as an example?
qa.a: Ujjwal holds up Bhavesh, his cousin's boy, who has a big job.

qa.q: How is Parveen feeling in this talk, and what does Parveen want?
qa.a: Parveen seems calm and determined, wanting a say without a quarrel; asking politely, offering to listen to the facts and saying "I have a mind" show it.

qa.q: What could Parveen do if the Saturday meeting does not change Ujjwal's mind?
qa.a: Keep asking respectfully for the reasons, perhaps bring another trusted elder as a bridge, and keep showing Ujjwal that listening goes both ways. ❤️

qa.q: Why might Ujjwal push the science stream so firmly?
qa.a: Ujjwal sees Bhavesh's big job as a safe future and probably wants that security for Parveen, which is why the choice came before the conversation.

grounding: A stream is being decided by a relative's success; Parveen stays respectful, asks for reasons and proposes a counsellor as a bridge.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Class 10, stream selection week

Akash came in on Monday looking flat. His father has filled in PCM for him because his cousin Kunal got into a top engineering college last year and the family talks about little else. Akash said, "I like biology and I love history. Nobody asked me." He was careful not to say anything rude about his father.

I suggested he ask for reasons rather than argue. He also asked if I could be in the room when he talked to his father.

On Thursday, Akash, his father and Kunal, home for the holidays, came in together. Akash asked, "Papa, can you tell me why PCM? I want to understand." His father talked about job security and respect. Then Kunal surprised us all: "Chacha, I chose engineering because I loved it. If Akash doesn't, he'll be miserable."

His father went quiet. We agreed Akash would sit in on biology and history classes for a week and decide with his parents on Monday.

qa.q: Who got into a top engineering college last year?
qa.a: Akash's cousin Kunal got into a top engineering college last year.

qa.q: What was Akash feeling when he said nobody asked him?
qa.a: Akash felt unheard and discouraged, but still careful and respectful about his father.

qa.q: What steps helped Akash speak up?
qa.a: Akash asked his father for reasons instead of arguing, and brought the counsellor into the room as a bridge.

qa.q: How might Akash's father feel after hearing Kunal?
qa.a: His father may feel surprised and unsure, realising the cousin's success came from interest, not just from choosing the right stream.

grounding: It shows a teen whose stream is being decided because of a relative's success, who stays respectful, asks for reasons and brings in a counsellor as a bridge.

passage:
Sunday night

Dadaji announced it at lunch today: I'm taking commerce. Because Zubin Chacha is a chartered accountant and "look how well he's done." Nobody looked at me. Papa just nodded.

I wanted to shout. I want to do science and maybe architecture. I kept eating and felt my face go hot. Having an opinion in this house feels like disobeying.

After lunch I went to Zubin Chacha on the balcony, since he's the one everyone keeps pointing to. I said, "Chacha, can I ask you something? Did you choose commerce, or did Dadaji choose it for you?" He laughed. "I chose it. I loved numbers since I was nine."

I told him I love building things. He listened. Then he said, "Let me talk to Dadaji with you. He listens to me on this."

We did it together at tea. I asked Dadaji, very politely, to tell me his reasons. He talked. Chacha talked. Dadaji said he'll think till Wednesday.

Not a yes. But not a no.

Abhinav

qa.q: What profession does Zubin Chacha have?
qa.a: Zubin Chacha is a chartered accountant.

qa.q: What was Abhinav feeling at lunch when Dadaji announced the stream?
qa.a: Abhinav felt angry and unheard, with a hot face, and felt that having an opinion was like disobeying.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Abhinav to go to Zubin Chacha first?
qa.a: Zubin Chacha was the example everyone used and a respected elder, so he could act as a bridge and help Abhinav ask Dadaji for reasons politely.

qa.q: How might Dadaji see the conversation at tea?
qa.a: Dadaji may feel a little surprised but respected, since Abhinav asked politely for reasons instead of fighting him.

grounding: It shows a teen whose stream is being decided because of a relative's success, who stays respectful, brings in an elder as a bridge and asks for reasons.
